name: Moxy
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult-only home.

I will need a kind, calm resident dog to show me the ropes. I'm unsure of cats.

I would like an extra-secure garden to spend time in.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I am currently in a foster home where I am learning about home life!

Moxy is a worried little girl who has come to us from a breeder and is now in foster, where she is beginning to show her lovely, affectionate personality. She can be unsure around new people, but as she learns to trust you, more of her sweet nature shines through. In the evenings, she will come to her fosterers for a cuddle on her own terms, which is lovely to see as she continues to grow in confidence.

Moxy will need an adult-only home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand that she needs time, patience and kindness to settle into her new life. A calm, quiet environment with minimal disruption will be important, as will having a gentle, quiet resident dog to help her feel safe and guide her through home life. Moxy has struggled with a more vocal dog in her foster home, so her canine companion will need to be calm and considerate of her needs.

Moxy has never lived in a home before and is learning about house training and everyday routines in foster. Her new family will need to continue this patiently and gently introduce her to lead walking. She has shown signs of digging, so she will also need an extra-secure garden to keep her safe.

Moxy arrived with sore eyes, and our vet noted that her lower eyelid is irregular, although this is not currently causing her any issues. We are also concerned that her vision is significantly reduced, as her depth perception seems affected. She may bump into things or be startled when other dogs approach unexpectedly, so her adopters will need to understand her visual difficulties and help her navigate her surroundings safely. She also arrived with sore skin and old concrete sores, which we hope will continue to improve.

Moxy has already made lovely progress and is gradually learning to trust the people around her. She will need a special family who can offer a peaceful home, a calm canine companion and the understanding she needs to feel secure. With time, patience and gentle reassurance, we hope this affectionate little girl will continue to blossom and discover just how lovely life can be.

Moxy has been on our section for a few weeks now & she is such a delight to be around.

Dependent on where Moxy is will decide which side of Moxy you will get. Both sides are a truly beautiful dog, but one is incredibly sad & shut down and the other is a wonderful, affectionate girl who truly tries her hardest to be brave.

When in the kennel you’ll find Moxy in the back, she’ll appear sad, broken & totally overwhelmed. She tries to dig a lot, and burrow herself behind any beds she can find. We have swapped these beds out with a big comfy duvet now where she likes to chill in the corner. However I do think she sees it as her safe space, where she will hide from the outside world. Once she’s out of that kennel, and running to the yard she will wag her body in its entirety as she greets other kennels desperately trying to make new friends.

Even in the yard, Moxy can still feel overwhelmed and will sit in the corner & dig at times, and we’ve even tried taking her out on a harness but she remains frozen. But once she’s comfortable in the company she is around, she is the most affectionate girl. She happily sits next to you, gives you kisses and that tail really does not stop wagging. Her company is joyous, and being one of her trusted people is so incredibly rewarding, and brightens every day I spend with her.

Moxy’s people will need to take it easy with her, need to understand exbreeders, and be patient & kind along her journey at home. Mixing her nervous character along with her poor eyesight, being at home is likely to be very scary for her. As one of her kennel mummies, I can vouch for her & tell you that gaining her trust, and gaining her as a family member will be the most fulfilling experience, and one I am extremely jealous of. Moxy deserves love, care & a place to feel safe after all this time feeling scared & overwhelmed.

Moxy, like a lot of ex breeder dogs, is a very nervous dog. When I first met her, she wouldn’t leave the back, didn’t want me to get near her and I had to carry her back and forth from the yard. On my second day with Moxy, she ran straight to the yard as I opened her kennel door and, once I entered the yard, she was jumping all over me, kissing me, genuinely thrilled to see me. This is behaviour that truly shocked me in the best possible way.

It’s now been a couple of weeks since I first worked with her and the affection she shows me and the confidence she found has only grown. She’s truly incredible.Around new people, she reverts back to shutting down and hiding in the back. Despite this, we still have an incredible relationship. Moxy needs to be shown she can trust you.

Once this girl trusts you, you’ll see the same side I see. You won’t see this side if you met her on a show around of our kennels or even if you were let in her kennel to socialise her. This is something you can only experience from adopting her and progressing her like we do. I truly love her with all my heart. Take a chance on her and I have no doubts you’ll experience the same as I.

Moxy is a very worried little girl who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is feeling quite overwhelmed to find herself here at the moment and is in need of lots of TLC, patience and reassurance. Once she gets to know you, she does start to come out of her shell and then enjoys a gentle fuss.

Moxy will need a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need plenty of time to settle in at her own pace. She will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help her learn how wonderful her life can be now. We would consider homing her with old, dog savvy teenagers.

Moxy has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her. Her new family will need to be kind and understanding as she learns all about home life, including new skills like house training and walking on a lead. She will need gentle encouragement and understanding as she settles in.

Moxy is a very sweet girl who has had a difficult start in life. She now needs someone who will give her the time, patience and love she needs to blossom. With a kind canine friend by her side and a quiet, understanding home, we hope she will slowly gain confidence and discover how lovely life can be.

Moxy has arrived with slightly sore eyes and our vet has noted her low eyelid is irregular but doesn't feel this is causing her any issues at the moment, but will need to be monitored moving forwards. Although she can see, her vision isn't the best, but she doesn't let this slow her down and gets around well. She also arrived with sore skin and old concrete sores, which will hopefully feel much better soon.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Jane
description:
I’d like an adult only home filled with love and kindness!

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I'm new to harness training and need some practice!

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I am receiving treatment for mastitis & I have a bilateral ear infection.

Jane is a sweet girl who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is a gentle, inquisitive little lady who is still shy around people, but she is very easy to handle and is beginning to show us that she wants to be brave. She will approach for gentle little sniffs and has started harness training, taking these small steps at her own pace.

Jane gets on wonderfully with all the dogs she has met and relies on their company for comfort and reassurance. She will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend, take her under their wing and help her learn all about home life.

Jane will need a calm, quiet adult only home with experienced adopters who understand scared ex-breeding dogs and will give her plenty of time, patience and TLC as she settles in. She needs kind, gentle people who will allow her to build confidence without pressure.

As Jane has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn about house training and the other basics of home life. She is still learning to wear a harness and will need continued, gentle encouragement with lead training, starting in the home and garden before gradually venturing further afield. We would consider sensible, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ in a suitable home.

Jane has arrived with mastitis and a bilateral ear infection, and she is currently receiving treatment. Her health will need to continue to be monitored, with any ongoing care provided as needed.

Jane is an adorable little lady who has so much potential. With a confident canine companion, a peaceful home and people who understand her needs, we hope she will continue to blossom and enjoy the happy new beginning she deserves.

Jane is just the most adorable little lady. She has a truly gentle and inquisitive nature, and despite being quite shy of us humans, she is very easy to handle. Jane has begun harness training and will approach for gentle little sniffs.

Jane gets on well with all the dogs she has met and is just an all-round lovely individual, seeking the lovely home she so deserves.

As Jane is still quite shy, she is best suited to an adult home where there will be at least one doggie companion to help show her the way and kind, gentle humans.

Jane is a sweet girl who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is feeling quite overwhelmed to find herself here at the moment and when you enter her kennel she will hide away in her bed, though if you do approach her she will let you handle her but is very worried about this. Once you leave her kennel, she will come up the front of it and will gently sniff you. She will need lots of love and TLC as she starts to come out of her shell.

Jane will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. We would consider homing her with dog savvy teenagers aged 16+.

She relies on other dogs for comfort and reassurance and so she will need a home where there is at least one other kind and confident resident dog to be her friend and take her under their wing. Having another confident dog to copy will help her settle into home life and will be really beneficial in helping grow her confidence.

As Jane has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to give her plenty of patience and encouragement while she gets used to everything that is new to her. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and will need to practice, first around the home and garden until she gains enough confidence to venture further.

Jane has arrived with mastitis and is currently receiving treatment with us. We will continue to monitor her closely to make sure she is comfortable and receiving the care she needs.

Jane is a gentle little girl who is already showing us small signs that she wants to be brave, and we hope that with the support of a confident canine companion and a kind, patient family, she will gradually gain confidence and enjoy the happy new start she deserves.

She is currently being treated for mastitis and a bilateral ear infection.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Tilly
description:
I can live with older dog-savvy children who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before

I've started my vaccinations and will be spayed before adoption.

22-10-26 Tilly is a very sweet but extremely nervous girly who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start.

Tilly will need plenty of time to settle into her new home, as she is not comfortable being handled at the moment. Her adopters will need to be patient and take things slowly, allowing her to go at her own pace so that she does not feel overwhelmed. She will need gentle encouragement and the chance to build trust in her own time.

Tilly will need another kind and confident dog in her new home. This dog will be a much-needed support system for her, helping to guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Tilly has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to understand that these things may take time and be willing to work with her at a pace she can manage.

Tilly's adopters will need to have ex-breeding experience to better understand her needs. She can live with older dog-savvy children that are sensible and understand she needs a quiet environment she can settle into. A calm environment, patient adopters and a reassuring canine companion will be important in helping her feel safe.

Tilly is a very worried little girl who will need understanding and patience to help her adjust to a new way of life. We hope that with the right support and plenty of time, she will gradually learn to trust and begin to enjoy the love and comfort of a home of her own.

Tilly has been given the Gift of Life by Laura Midwinter-Brown

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Sky
description:
I can live with older, calm teens aged, 13+ who allow me time to settle in.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I walk well on lead but I can be spooked. Let's take it slow!

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

I am underweight and healing from mastitis. Please read below for more!

Sky is an outrageously beautiful little Poodle cross who has come to us from a breeder and is now settling into foster life. She was incredibly frightened when she first arrived but has made lovely progress and is becoming much more comfortable with people. She is now happy to be handled and will come looking for fuss when she feels confident. Sky can still be startled by things around her, but she settles well with gentle reassurance and is learning that the world isn't such a scary place.

Sky is a social little girl who loves the company of other dogs and will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help her continue building her confidence. She will suit a quiet household with experienced adopters who understand nervous ex-breeding dogs and will give her the time she needs to settle without pressure. We would consider a home with sensible, dog-savvy teenagers aged 13+ who will respect her need for space.

Sky has been doing brilliantly with her house training and has been completely clean in the home from day one! She also sleeps peacefully in her cosy crate overnight without making a peep. She walks well on a lead, and we would love to see her continue developing this skill with her adopters.

Sky arrived underweight and with mastitis and bilateral dermatitis. Thankfully, her mastitis has now completely cleared, and the small areas of dermatitis in her lip folds are much improved. She is a very good girl when these areas are cleaned, and keeping this up as part of her grooming routine is helping them heal quickly. She also enjoys being brushed! Sky is still underweight, so she will need a nutritious diet and continued monitoring as she gradually reaches a healthy weight.

Sky has come such a long way and is showing us more of her lovely personality as she grows in confidence. With a calm home, a kind canine companion and plenty of patience, we believe this beautiful girl will continue to blossom.

Sky has been given the Gift of Life by Ruth Butterworth

Sky has had a great first week in foster. She has settled in well and is starting to really enjoy home comforts! Her mastitis has all gone, and the small areas of dermatitis in her lip folds are much improved. She is a very good girl when I clean them for her. With continued good hygiene, they are rapidly clearing up. We have made it part of her grooming routine, and she doesn’t mind being brushed at all. She is still underweight, but we are building her up slowly.

Sky met the other dogs really well and is gentle and unassuming with them. She will need another kind dog in her new home.

Sky bonded with me very quickly. She follows me around and is never happier than when she is snuggled on my lap! A real cuddler. She is nervous of the rest of the family but will allow them to approach and handle her.

This is Sky’s first experience of home life. At first, she was scared of the TV and household noises, but she’s adjusting really quickly. She has been out for a little walk and was curious and excited on our quiet route, sniffing the grass and exploring. She has been totally clean from day one and sleeps in her cosy crate without a peep overnight.

This blondie has the potential to be a wonderful companion and, with time and love, will really blossom. I hope her people find her soon; she deserves her happy ever after.

Sky is an outrageously beautiful poodle cross. When she came to us, she was petrified. She was terrified of humans, hid in the back of the kennel, and would only eat if she was shut in the back (it was her safe space). To be able to get close enough to touch her felt impossible.

With time, Sky has really come out of her shell. She’s still nervous, especially of new people; however, we have cuddles now. I am a trusted person in her eyes. With time, you could be too.

As she now allows me to stroke her, cuddle her and pick her up, we decided she’d made enough progress to go for a walk.

I fitted her with a harness, leaded her and her kennel friend up (so she’d have a confident friend for guidance) and, to my surprise, she walked like she’d been doing it for years! Noises scared her a little, so did the lead when she pulled it tight. She likes the slack. Other than that, perfect.

I’m so proud of this girl. The progress I’ve seen her make is incredible. Seeing where she is now compared to when I first met her, it genuinely brings a tear (of joy) to my eye.

Sky is a ridiculously beautiful, small poodle cross. She definitely needs a resident dog to keep the progress flowing. Are you the home for Sky? Read the rest of her profile above to get a fuller picture.

Sky is a very scared little lady who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She can be skittish and quite shut down at the moment so she will need a calm home. Sky prefers to hide at the back of her kennel and finds handling very frightening. She trembles when she is being handled and can't wait to be safely back on the floor, where she will quickly run back to her bed. We know she doesn't understand yet that we are here to help her, so she will need lots of time and patience to learn that she is safe.

Sky will need another kind and confident dog in the home, and this dog will be a much-needed support system for her. Having a friendly dog by her side should help her feel more secure and give her someone to follow as she begins to discover the world outside the kennel.

As Sky has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life. Her adopters will need to be very patient and allow her to take everything at her own pace.

We are looking for a quiet, patient home for Sky so that she can relax and settle into her new surroundings without too much hustle and bustle. She will need adopters who understand scared ex-breeding dogs and who are prepared to give her the time she needs without putting any pressure on her. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens, aged 13+ who are sensible and will allow her time to settle in at her own pace.

Sky has arrived very underweight and with mastitis. She is healing well so far, but will need a nutritious diet to help her reach and maintain a healthy weight going forward. She has bilateral dermatitis that will need to be cleaned. This will need to be continued in her new home, and her adopters will need to keep an eye on her progress.

Sky has a long way to go, but underneath all that fear is a little dog who deserves the chance to feel safe and loved. With the right home, a kind canine companion and lots of patience, we hope she will slowly begin to blossom and discover how wonderful life can be.

name: Crush
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I walk well on a harness and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home before so know the basics.

I have bilateral nuclear sclerosis. Please read below for more information!

Crush is a sweet gentleman who has come to us from a breeder and is still waiting for his forever home. After spending all his life breeding, he is now finally getting to experience the love and kindness he deserves, and his confidence has truly blossomed during his time with us. He has learned to walk on a lead and is doing so well, showing us just how much he has to offer!

Crush is a lovely, chilled and laid-back boy who gets on wonderfully with other dogs. He gets super excited when meeting new friends out on walks and can turn into a playful pup, which is so lovely to see! He also enjoys a good run around in the yards with his kennel friends before settling down again. Crush can happily live with other resident dogs, and in the right home, we feel he could possibly be an only dog too.

Crush has also been a little star for his bath and groom, happily allowing himself to be scrubbed, blow-dried and even having a little face trim. He really is a fluffy white ball of perfection! He will make a lovely companion for someone looking for a gentle, easygoing boy to share their home with.

Crush has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be patient as he learns about house training and adjusts to a new routine. He could live with dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who understand that he may need some time to settle into his new surroundings. With his lovely progress so far, we hope he will continue to grow in confidence and enjoy all the little things that make home life so special.

Crush has bilateral nuclear sclerosis, which will need to be monitored in his new home, although it does not appear to bother him at present. He also has the potential for chronic skin issues and dental disease that will need to be monitored, and he has already had two teeth extracted while with us.

Crush has spent so many years waiting for his chance to be loved, and now we desperately hope someone will see what a wonderful boy he is. He has so much love to give and deserves to spend his golden years enjoying the comforts of a forever home, with a cosy bed, kind people and all the love he has missed out on for so long.

Crush has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

How is this sweet gentleman still waiting for his home? At 9 years old, Crush wants nothing more than a place to call home. He’s spent all his years breeding until finally arriving with us where he has been showered with love, met new friends and even to walk lead! His confidence truly has bloomed in the last few months.

He is perfect around other dogs and gets super excited when meeting others out on walks and turns into a playful pup. He’s a very chilled and laid back boy but he does enjoy a good run around in the yards with his friends.

Crush had a bath and groom with me a few days ago and he was perfect. He allowed me to scrub him down and also blow dry him before giving him a little face trim.

The boy truly is a fluffy white ball of perfection!

Crush can live with other resident dogs and in the right home could possibly be an only.

Crush is a fairly nervous boy who has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for a loving forever home. He can be very shy and tends to rely heavily on his kennel friends for comfort and reassurance, so he will need time and patience as he settles into his new surroundings.

Crush will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in the home that he can look to and lean on as he learns about home life and begins to build his confidence. He has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be understanding as he learns all about house training and adjusts to a new routine.

Crush is walking well on a harness, so he would enjoy one or two walks around the local area with the resident dog when he is settled in.

He could live with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who understand that he will need plenty of time and space to settle in and begin to trust. Crush is a lovely boy who simply needs plenty of TLC, patience, and kindness as he finds his paws in the world.

He has come to us with bilateral nuclear sclerosis that will need to be monitored in his new home, and does not seem to bother him at this time. The vet has noted that he has a potential for chronic skin issues and dental disease that will need to be monitored in his new home. He has had two teeth extracted with us.

name: Pebble
description:
I’d like an active home filled with love and kindness!

I could live with other dogs, or be the only dog. I don't mind. I haven’t met cats

I'm new to lead walking and need some practice!

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before

My lip folds and ears will need constant monitoring and cleaning! I have been spayed.

20-10-26 Pebble is a lovely, friendly lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is a very pretty girl with attractive colouring and lots of energy. Pebble gets on well with other dogs, loves attention from people and is easy to handle, making her a lovely girl to have around.

Pebble could happily live with another friendly dog for companionship or be the only dog in her new home, where she can enjoy plenty of attention from her people.

As Pebble has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. She is new to lead walking, so her adopters will need to give her some practice and encouragement as she learns to enjoy walks and explore the world beyond the garden.

Pebble could live with dog-savvy children aged 9 and over who understand the importance of giving her a gentle introduction to her new home and allowing her space to settle.

Pebble's lip folds and ears will need regular, ongoing monitoring and cleaning to keep them healthy and comfortable. Her adopters must be prepared to continue this care as part of her routine.

Pebble is a happy, energetic girl who enjoys human attention and the company of other dogs. With a loving family, plenty of affection and patience as she adjusts to home life, we hope she will thrive and make the most of her wonderful new start.

name: Milo
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands me.

I will need to be the only dog in my new home, so all of the attention is on me!

I will need an extra secure garden, at least 6ft+ where I will be safe!

I walk well on a lead but will need my adopters to be understanding of my needs!

I have lived in a home before so may I may already know the basics.

I will be neutered before finding my forever home!

06-10-26 Milo is a super sweet boy who has come to us from a home through no fault of his own. Sadly, he has already been through more changes than a young dog should have to, and he is understandably a little worried in new environments. He takes a lot of comfort from people he knows, but once he feels comfortable, his fun and affectionate personality really starts to shine.

Milo is an incredibly sweet boy who absolutely loves being close to his people and thinks he is the perfect lap dog! He is happiest when he can have a cuddle and will happily climb up for a lap sit. He is a sensitive little soul and will need a kind and patient home where he can continue to build his confidence and learn that he is safe and secure.

Milo will be looking for a home where he can be the only dog and get all the fuss and attention for himself. We are told that he has had a previous incident with a cat and so he cannot be homed with cats or small furries and must be kept on lead unless in a secure area.

Milo has missed out on some socialisation, but he is currently working on his social skills and is making lovely progress. He can happily walk alongside calm dogs and has had some nice greetings. He doesn't always know what to make of other dogs yet and can sometimes get a little carried away when mixing, but with continued positive socialisation we are sure his confidence will grow. He can also react if another dog barks at him first while on lead, so his new family will need to understand this and help him learn how to navigate these situations.

Milo will need an adult-only home with people who have experience of bull breeds and understand what sensitive souls they can be.Although he is a wonderful boy, he would not be suitable for a first time dog owner.He will need a kind and patient family who can give him time to settle and continue building his confidence. He will also need the time he is left home alone built up gradually as he settles into his new home.

Milo will need an extra secure garden of at least 6ft to keep him safe, as he is a young and active boy who could be an escape artist if given the opportunity.

Milo is such a lovely young boy who has already been through so much change. With the right family, patience and continued socialisation, we know he will make a wonderful companion and be the loving, fun little lap dog he is so desperate to be.

name: Kismet
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I am spayed and have had an umbilical hernia repaired.

Kismet is a lovely girl who came to us from a breeder and has now moved to a wonderful foster home, where she is experiencing life in a home for the very first time. She has a sweet, gentle nature and is a curious, active little girl who is slowly finding her feet and learning that the world isn't such a scary place.

Kismet is still a little unsure of people, but she is making a lovely start in foster. She enjoys following her fosterer around and is happy to accept a gentle fuss, although she isn't quite brave enough to ask for attention herself just yet. She is beginning to settle into her new routine and sleeps quietly overnight snuggled up in a crate with her foster buddy, greeting her fosterer each morning with a lovely waggy tail. These little moments show that she is trying her best, and with time, patience and kindness, we hope she will continue to grow in confidence.

Kismet takes great comfort from the company of other dogs and will need a kind, friendly resident dog of a similar size in her new home. She would love a canine companion who enjoys snuggling up and sharing their bed, as having other dogs around helps her feel safe and secure while she gets used to her new surroundings.

Kismet is doing well with her toilet training when given regular opportunities to go out into the garden. She has also started learning to wear a harness, but she will need more time to build her confidence before beginning to learnt to walk on a lead, which can initially be introduced gently in the garden when she feels ready.

Kismet arrived with us very underweight, so she is currently being fed three meals a day in a crate to ensure she gets all the food she needs without her canine friends helping themselves! It will be important for her to continue enjoying a nutritious diet in her new home to help her reach and maintain a healthy weight. She also had a small umbilical hernia, which was repaired at the time of her spay.

As this is Kismet's first experience of living in a home, she will need patient adopters who understand that everything is new to her and who will give her the time and encouragement she needs to settle at her own pace. She will also need someone around for most of the day while she adjusts to her new routine, with any time left alone introduced gradually as she becomes more confident. Kismet can live with sensible, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who will understand her need for patience and reassurance.

Kismet is making a lovely start in foster and has so much potential to blossom into a happy, confident little companion. With a loving family, a reassuring canine friend and plenty of patience, we hope she will continue to discover just how wonderful life in a home can be and find the forever home she deserves.

Kismet has been given the Gift of Life by Margaret Hunter

Kismet has made a good start in foster. She has a sweet gentle nature, is curious, active, shadows her fosterer and sleeps quietly at night with her foster buddy Kylie in a crate, and greets me in the morning with a lovely waggy tail.

Kismet is underweight and is fed 3 meals a day in a crate so that she doesn’t allow the rest of the pack to help her out. With regular visits to the garden she is doing well with toilet training.

Harness training has started but lead walking will wait until she is more confident and then start in the garden. Kismet will accept a gentle fuss but does not ask for attention yet.

Kismet needs a home with at least one similar size playmate who likes to cosy up and share their bed as she takes great comfort from their presence and owners where someone is around most of the time while she settles into a new routine. Time alone will have to be built up gradually.

Kismet is a lovely, happy girl who has come into our care from a breeder. She is a semi-brave little girl who wants to be our friend, but just can't quite get there yet. If we need to pick her up, Kismet will lie down and accept the handling, and she will offer little kisses on our hands while wagging her tail. These small signs show that she is trying her best, even though she is still a little unsure.

Kismet gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Kismet has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to give her plenty of time, patience and encouragement while she gets used to her new surroundings. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who are sensible and will allow her time to settle in.

Kismet has arrived very underweight, so she will need a nutritious diet to help her reach and maintain a healthy weight. This will need to be continued in her new home. She also has a small umbilical hernia, which has been repaired at the time of her spay.

Kismet is a sweet little girl who is clearly trying hard to be brave, and we hope that with the support of a kind canine companion and a loving, patient family, she will slowly gain confidence and discover just how lovely life in a home can be.

name: Otis
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden with 6ft+ fences.

I have started harness training, but this is still new to me!

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home!

Otis has come to us from a breeder to find his forever home. He is an extremely nervous boy who is still finding the world a very scary place and is utterly petrified of human touch. When he first arrived, he would do everything he could to avoid being touched, frantically running around the yard to escape contact. Although he was interested in people, he simply didn't feel brave enough to let them close.

Otis is now making small but lovely steps forward, although he is still extremely worried about touch, with those who he knows very well he will tentatively accept chin tickles, though is still very worried about this. He still needs to build his confidence, and getting him comfortable with human hands will be a slow process that is likely to continue well into his new home. His adopters must be prepared to work at his pace, without rushing or putting pressure on him.

At just one year old, Otis has plenty of typical Labrador puppy character waiting to shine through. He loves tennis balls and soft toys and is still figuring out how to play fetch! As his confidence grows, we're beginning to see more of his funny, silly personality, and we hope there is lots more to come.

Otis absolutely adores other dogs and takes great comfort and reassurance from their company. He will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in his new home to help him feel safe and guide him as he learns about life in a home. Having a canine friend by his side will be particularly important while he continues to build trust in people.

Otis will need a calm, quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and understand the time and patience they need. He has never lived in a home before, so he will need help learning all about home life, including house training. He will also need a secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft to keep him safe while he gains confidence.

Otis has started harness training with his kennel mummy, and this will need to continue in his home at a slow and comfortable pace. This will need to be introduced gradually, starting in a safe environment and allowing him to progress at his own pace.

Otis is a special little boy who is trying so hard to be brave. With patient, understanding adopters and a confident canine companion, we believe he has the potential to blossom into a fun, loving and rewarding companion. He will need a family willing to celebrate the smallest steps forward and give him the time he needs to discover that the world can be a wonderful place.

Otis has been given the Gift of Life by Nic Johhston

Otis is a few weeks into his stay at Many Tears and honestly, he’s breaking my heart. That being said, he is progressing slowly, in his own funny way.

Otis is utterly petrified of human touch and when he first arrive he would do literally anything to get away from me. I mean truly frantic to avoid being touched. He would bolt away in the yard and do laps to avoid any contact. He wouldn’t take treats from my hand despite being a massive foodie! Yet when I turned around he would show interest to me and would nibble my hand through the gates. He so wanted to be brave and just didn’t know how.

We are slowly getting there, it’s not much of a progression to most people but he will freeze with me now and tentatively accept chin tickles. Small baby steps, we are already seeing progress! Desensitising Otis to human hands is not going to be a quick fix and will likely continue into his home life. He does now take treats from my hand, even in the yard but after each treat he does a little lap of the yard to ramp himself up for the next one! He really is such a funny little guy.

At just 1 years old, he has so much of your typical Lab puppy in him, but he just doesn’t feel safe enough to fully let it out. He loves a tennis ball and is still coming to grips with how fetch works. He loves soft toys and ADORES the company of other dogs and seeks so much comfort and support from them.

Once Otis is more comfortable being handled, our next milestone will be getting him in a harness to begin the road to exploring the world on walks!

He is such a character & the more confident he becomes, the more we get to see his funny, silly side. I really do believe he will settle into the most fulfilling, fun dog you could hope for & will make his future adopters very happy!

Otis has come to us from a breeder to find his forever home. He is a very nervous boy who is feeling very overwhelmed by all the changes in his life and is finding his surroundings quite scary at the moment. He is very worried about being handled and it is clear that he has not had much socialisation before, so he is in need of lots of patience, kindness and TLC.

Otis will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and understand that he will need plenty of time to settle in and build his confidence at his own pace. He will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in his new home to be his friend and companion and help show him the ropes. Having a confident canine friend by his side will be very important as Otis begins to learn that the world is not such a scary place.

Otis will also need a secure garden with 6ft+ fencing to keep him safe while he gains confidence. He has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be kind and understanding as he learns all about home life and new skills such as house training.

Otis doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and this will need to be introduced very gradually by practicing first in the garden, allowing him to gain confidence before venturing further afield.

Otis is a very worried boy who needs someone special to give him the time and understanding he deserves. With a calm environment, a confident canine companion and lots of patience and love, we hope that little by little he will begin to feel safe and discover the happy boy hiding underneath all those worries.

name: Eve
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

I am learning to walk on a lead and harness, but it's still very new for me.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

Eve is a sweet girl who has come to us from a breeder ready to find her forever home. When she first arrived she was a very scared little girl who was understandably finding the world quite overwhelming.

Eve has recently moved to a wonderful foster home where she is getting to experience home life for the first time and it has been such a joy watching her settle in to home life. Her confidence has progressed incredibly and given where she started, her resilience and curiosity are nothing short of amazing. She can still be a bit skittish around sudden movements, but is doing so well.

Eve does gain confidence from other dogs and would love to have another kind and confident resident dog in her new home, however in the right circumstances with experienced adopters who have plenty of time to spend with her, we would consider homing her as an only dog. She does value her personal space and isn't keen on sharing her bed with other dogs and can guard it from them, so it will be essential that her adopters would be happy to manage this behaviour and work on it with her.

Eve loves her food and a slow feeder bowl is an absolute must for her, otherwise she’d clear her plate in seconds. She’s also masterfully tuned in to the household and already knows the exact sound of the snack cupboards opening and the rustle of a crisp packet!

She tackled learning the stairs almost immediately and navigates them like a pro now. Her toilet training and walking on a lead nad harness are coming along nicely, though they will just need a bit of ongoing, gentle guidance in her forever home as she continues to build routine and confidence.

Eve will be best suited to a calm and quiet home where she can continue to settle in and progress at her own pace, but with time, love and kindness we think she will truly blossom into the most wonderful girl.

She has some sore and inflamed paw pads when she first arrived at the rescue and also has a travel document.

Eve has been given the Gift of Life by Anne Breen

Meet Eve: The Sweet, Confident Cocker Spaniel Looking for Her Forever Home!

Eve came into foster care with us almost four weeks ago, and it has been such a joy watching her settle into home life!

I’ve owned and fostered many Cocker Spaniels over the years, and Eve stands out as one of the most delightfully confident ones I’ve met. Because of her background, she can still be a bit skittish or nervous around sudden movements, but given where she started, her resilience and curiosity are nothing short of amazing.

Here is a little glimpse into life with Eve:

Dog-Friendly & Independent: She shares her foster home with a whole pack of dogs and gets along fine with everyone. That said, she values her personal space especially when it comes to her bed! (Honestly, who amongst us likes sharing a mattress?) She would thrive living either as an only dog or alongside other canine companions. She’s also quite independent and comfortable being left happily for a few hours.

Foodie at Heart: Eve loves her food! A slow feeder bowl is an absolute must for her, otherwise she’d clear her plate in seconds. She’s also masterfully tuned in to the household—she already knows the exact sound of the snack cupboards opening and the rustle of a crisp packet!

Household Progress: She tackled learning the stairs almost immediately and navigates them like a pro now. Her toilet training and lead/harness walking are coming along nicely, though they will just need a bit of ongoing, gentle guidance in her forever home as she continues to build routine and confidence.

Eve is an absolute beauty inside and out. She is ready for a patient, loving home where she can continue to blossom into the wonderful companion she’s proving to be.

Eve is a nervous girl who has come into our care from a breeder.

She is a very scared little girl who is understandably finding the world quite overwhelming. Eve relies heavily on the comfort of her doggy friends and is currently very skittish. She is a flight risk, so her new family will need to take great care to ensure she always feels safe and secure while she settles into her new life.

Eve will need another kind, confident dog in the home to take her under their wing and be a much-needed support system to help guide her, build her confidence, and reassure her as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Eve has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding, allowing her to progress at her own pace without any pressure.

Eve is looking for a calm, adult-only home with confident adopters who understand that building trust will take time. A secure garden and a confident resident dog will be essential to help her adjust safely and gently to home life.

Eve is a gentle soul who has a long journey ahead of her, but every small step forward will be a huge achievement. With time, patience, and the support of a confident canine companion, we hope she will gradually discover that the world isn't such a scary place after all.

She is currently being monitored for sore and inflamed paw pads, and this will need to be monitored in her new home.

name: Tummy
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teenagers, aged 13+ who respect my space.

I will need to be the only dog in the home so all of the attention is on me!

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have previously lived in a home, so I may already know the basics!

I am on a special diet for bladder stones, please read below for more information!

11-10-26 Tummy is a lovely lady who originally came to us from a breeder and was later adopted into a home. Sadly, she has returned to our care after around 5 months as she wasn't getting along with the resident dog, so she is now looking for a home where she can be the only dog and have all of her family's attention to herself. She also cannot live with cats or small furries.

Tummy is a sweet and outgoing girl with a big personality! She loves toys and having a good play, but she also enjoys a quiet fuss and relaxing alongside her people. She has lived in a home before, so she may already know some of the basics such as house training, although she may need a few gentle reminders as she settles back into home life.

Tummy would do best with a family who has experience with Dachshunds and understands their wonderful but sometimes strong personalities, although she could also live with a sensible family who are willing to learn and understand her needs. She can live with dog-savvy teenagers aged 13+ who are sensible and will give her the time and space she needs to settle into her new home.

Tummy has never been left home alone before and so this is something her adopters will need to build up gradually with her to ensure she doesn't develop separation anxiety.

Tummy is an amazing little lady who has already had a change of home and is now ready to find her forever family. We hope that the right home will give her the love, attention and stability she deserves.

Tummy has previously been treated for ear infections and also has some hair loss that seemed to begin to grow back when she was in her previous home. She has a history of bladder stones and is currently on a specific diet to help with this, and this will need to be continued in the home. This will need to be monitored by her new vets and her adopters will need to be aware that should she require any treatment or potential surgery in the future it would not be covered by insurance.

Hungry has been given the Gift of Life by Jacqueline Wanstall

name: Sheamy
description:
I can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who understand I need space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have been neutered and had 19 teeth removed.

22-10-26 Sheamy is a shy boy who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. He is a timid little chap who allows us to approach him for a gentle fuss, although he is not yet confident enough to come over to us himself. He is much livelier when he is with his kennel friends, and it is lovely to see him feeling more comfortable in their company.

Sheamy gets on wonderfully with his kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so he will need a kind resident dog in his new home, ideally a female, to help guide him and give him the reassurance he needs as he settles in and finds his paws.

Sheamy has been neutered and had 19 teeth removed at the time of his neutering.

name: Lassie
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog Cocker Spaniel size or larger in my new home. No cats please!

I would like a secure garden with 6ft boundariesto spend time in.

I can walk well on a lead and would love an active home.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home.

Lassie has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. When she first arrived she was overwhelmed by absolutely everything, especially people. She had very little trust in humans in general which meant her kennel humans had to put in a lot of time and effort in to gaining her trust and helping her grow her circle. When meeting new people she needs to put distance between her and them until she decides that she is comfortable enough to approach them. If the person was to make Lassie feel trapped then she may growl or bark to ask for distance.

Once she has a bond with you she becomes the most affectionate, attentive, loyal and loving dog to have as a companion. Lassie will need a resident dog in her new home and since arriving she has had a variety of kennel friends, including a Bernese, Pomskis, Collie, and Beagle. She is also yarded with a mixture of other dogs and does well with them all. She does seem to prefer Collies and would love a Collie friend in her new home, but she could be homed with any dog that is no smaller than a Cocker, as she does find little dogs very fun to herd.

Due to Lassie’s past she is looking for a home with no cats, small furries or livestock and adopters who will never let her off lead anywhere near sheep fields as she is fixated with them, not surprisingly due to her breed. Lassie must always be kept safe from making the wrong decisions.

Lassie has never lived in a home before so her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she settles in and learns all about home life as well as new skills like house training.

In the right home Lassie will thrive. She doesn't cope well in busy environments, so someone who enjoys quiet country walks with her would be a great fit.  Things like busy cafes and pubs would be far too much for her at the moment and she may never enjoy those things, so her prospective new family will need to bare that in mind when considering bringing her into their home.

Lassie is a very smart girl who does pick up new things quickly when in a calm and stress free environment. She has learnt 'sit', 'down' and is currently learning 'touch'. She also sits beautifully on the grass verge when waiting for cars to go past on her walks. Walks really are her favourite thing, whenever her harness comes out her whole body can't help but wag but can still be startled by traffic and loud noises.

She is a girl who does require patience and understanding, especially in the beginning, but she gives you so much in return and will make someone very lucky indeed.

Lassie will need more than one meet and greet with her prospective adopters to allow her time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Lassie has been in foster for a week now and is making lovely progress every day! She is still a nervous girl who startles easily, but she is beginning to come out of her shell and will now approach her foster family for fuss. She absolutely loves belly rubs and greets them each morning with a lovely waggy tail!

She gets on brilliantly with the three resident dogs, enjoying running around and playing ball with her new friends. Lassie is also learning all about house training and is doing well. She loves her food and treats, sleeps quietly through the night in her bedroom crate with the door open, and is a wonderful passenger in the car. She happily jumps in and out and enjoys watching the world go by through the window.

Lassie walks well on the lead but can still be startled by traffic and loud noises, so she will need patient adopters who understand nervous Collies and can help her build confidence at her own pace.

Lassie will need a secure garden and a kind, confident resident dog to help her feel safe. She is looking for a home without children or cats, where she can continue to blossom with time, patience and understanding.

Lassie has proved to us, once Lassie knows and trusts you, she will be a friend for life.

Lassie is doing absolutely amazing at making doggy friends lately. She has been socialising with Cockers, Springer crosses, a large Cav, and her kennel friend is a Pomsky now. To start, she is a bit wary but does settle okay if they're not too in her face and allow her to just exist around them for a while. She's the most affectionate girl when she knows you well, but bonding with new people is a slow process, and her new people will really need to understand all of her quirks and be willing to put in the time to help her trust them.

Lassie walks well with her trusted people and will happily walk for miles and miles. She will also settle in her chosen human's presence well, and she does know how to relax here in kennels too.

I cannot express how much I adore this girl, and the loyalty and love she gives you once you've earned a spot in her trusted circle is beyond anything I can begin to describe. She's just incredible.

I took Lassie off-site to the Black Mountain Range. Kennels are no place for an energetic collie, so we set off on a 6.5km hike.

We set off, and the first thing that surprised me was how well she settled in the car. She was good as gold. Quietly and calmly sat still, occasionally getting up to look through the window. Given she is your standard high-energy collie, and the energy she exerts in kennels, I expected her to be majorly fidgety and unsettled. Boy, was I wrong, perfect passenger princess.

Once we began the hike, she instantly diverted to sniffs. Obviously, I allow her all the sniffs she wants. A 2-year-old collie that has been with us over a year, of course I want her to experience all these new scents she’s never smelt before!

Along the way, she decided she wanted to frolic and roll in some wildflowers, so naturally I joined her. We stopped, had a 5 min rest, some water and treats, before continuing.

Not far after, we encountered some sheep. Lassie did indeed stalk the sheep. She was double-leaded at all times, so this was not an issue. It must be said, Lassie is not a dog that should be off-lead right now. She can definitely be a flight risk and, if she starts herding sheep on farmers' land...

On the way back down, we ran for about 1.5km. She thoroughly enjoyed this!

She was the perfect hiking companion. All in all, 6.5km hike with 400m elevation in 1h15mins, and she was just as full of energy at the end as she was to begin. Safe to say, collies NEED that daily opportunity to alleviate some of that “crazy collie energy”!

I gave her paws a quick clean, gave her a dental stick for the journey home (it didn’t last 1/4 of the way back), and we returned to the rescue for dinner. Successful outing with the most incredible collie!

Lassie spent some time in the office today and coped really well. She happily tucked into a chicken foot for a tasty treat, although she couldn't resist pinching her kennel friend's one too! She was very curious about everything going on around her and enjoyed exploring her surroundings.

A member of staff she hadn't met before came into the office, and although Lassie was a little wary at first, she quickly settled and went back to happily enjoying her chicken foot. It was lovely to see her take the new experience in her stride and continue growing in confidence.

Beautiful beautiful Lassie! What a collie she is, she is so bright and has really come on so much with her basic training. Now knowing "sit" and "lie down". When we're out walking and a car is approaching, all I have to do is ask her to the verge and she sits and waits beautifully until we're able to start walking again. She really doesn't seem to be fazed by much traffic, but is very fixated with sheep if she comes across any. She passes horses lovely and will happily walk past other dogs no issue, but isn't keen on them approaching her. She's a big fan of food which helps with her training.She just needs people that understand that the girl she is when they first meet her is very worried but once she trusts you, her true personality really shines through.

Lassie is such a pretty girl who would do anything for you when she trusts you but is still wary of people initially. She did take treats off of a new person yesterday which was amazing to see. She needs to be in a collie experienced home with someone who will allow her the time to trust them at her own pace. She does love having a playfriend and she seems to be happiest when amongst other collies and collie crosses. She doesn't like sharing her food but is happy to share toys, beds and treats.

Lassie absolutely loves going out for her walks and gets very excited when she knows it’s time to head out. She really enjoys having a good sniff along the way and is always very interested in watching what’s going on in the fields as she passes by. Once she gets to know you, she is incredibly loving and affectionate, although she can take a little bit of time to warm up to new people. Lassie would still need a home with a resident dog, and she would truly thrive in a collie-experienced home where her needs and personality can be well understood.

Lassie is such a beautiful girl and once she knows you, she is the most affectionate, loyal and loving companion. She now walks well on a lead and absolutely loves her walks.

She will need a home with at least one other kind and confident resident dog who is a similar size to her and who loves to have a good play sometimes.

She doesn't like to share her food bowl, so he will need to be fed separately and this is something that her adopters will need to manage. In the right home she'll be someone's absolute best friend.

Lassie is a worried little lady who has come to us from a breeder. She has not had much experience with people, so everything feels very new and overwhelming to her. She can be quite skittish when approached, so she will need a calm, experienced home where she can be given the time and patience she needs to learn to trust.

At the moment, Lassie is scared of being touched, but she has already started to build a bond with her kennel mum and now allows gentle strokes from her. This shows that with consistency and kindness, shecanlearn to trust, and once she feels safe, she will begin to show her sweet side.

Lassie does walk on a lead, though she finds new experiences worrying, so she will need gentle introductions to the big wide world. She will also need to learn about house training and all the basics of living in a home, as these are things she has never known before.

Because Lassie is such a sensitive soul, she will need an adult-only home with no visiting children, and adopters who are happy to take things slowly at her pace. She will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can help her feel secure and show her the ropes. She gets on brilliantly with all dogs here and socialises well with a variety of breeds and sizes. She cannot be homed with cats or small furries.

With time, patience, and lots of love, Lassie will blossom. Once she has settled and gained confidence, she will become a cracking addition to her new family and will enjoy all the adventures life has to offer.

Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Alice
description:
I need an adult only home that can understand me and provide me with plenty of TLC.

I'd like to live with a resident dog my size and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden with 6ft fencing while I get used to my new home.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have been spayed, please read below for more information!

12-10-26 Alice originally came to us from a breeder a few months ago, she was adopted but sadly she struggled to settle into the home and would chose to stay in her crate and wouldn't move freely around the home and so her adopters made the decision to return her to our care after a short adoption. She went straight into a foster home and has now spent two months there settling in.

Alice's foster family have worked patiently to help her build confidence at her own pace. A comfortable dog bed was gradually moved into the busier areas of the house, allowing Alice to become accustomed to everyday family life while still having a safe space of her own.

Initially, Alice found it difficult to remain in a room if her fosterer moved or walked past her. This has improved enormously, and she will now often stay in the room, even when people move around her. In the evenings, she is relaxed enough to settle with the family while they watch television.

Within the home she continues to be “hand shy” unless initiated by herself which is usually a quick lick of your hand.

Out on walks, Alice is an absolute superstar! The moment she sees her lead, she transforms into an excited, happy girl, wagging her tail in anticipation. She is a pleasure to walk alongside her three canine companions, and this is where her confidence and loving nature really shine. When outside on her lead she allows gentle cuddles, takes treats from your hand and is increasingly able to relax and enjoy the world around her. She needs two walks a day to allow for this interaction time.

Alice would love a calm, patient, adult only home with one friendly dog of a similar size to help her feel secure and with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs. She has shown a particular preference for the Labrador in her foster home, whose companionship she clearly enjoys. She will also need a garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

Alice sometimes chooses to sleep away from her fosterers upstairs, but she has a charming way of persuading another dog to settle nearby in the hallway on their beds. Her need for canine companionship is clear, and having a trusted dog friend appears to bring her comfort.

Alice is not looking for a home where everything has to happen at once. She needs a family willing to give her time, reassurance and the freedom to grow in confidence without pressure. She also needs the companionship of another suitable dog and a home where her family are available for regular, gentle interaction throughout the day.

Alice has a continuing journey of discovering trust and the joy that comes with it .

Alice arrived with a cyst on her last mammary gland, which was drained during her spay surgery.
