name: Pushkin
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on harness but I can be spooked. Let's take it slow!

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home. Read below for more information!

Pushkin has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for a loving forever home. She can be nervous when meeting new people and situations, but her confidence has grown so much during her time with us. She simply needs a little time to warm up and figure people out, and once she feels comfortable her wonderful personality starts to shine through.

Pushkin is a truly lovely girl with a fun, quirky nature and a very affectionate side. She has become a firm favourite with the staff who know her, and once she trusts you she is incredibly rewarding to spend time with. She loves being around people she knows and has a gentle, sweet temperament that is impossible not to fall in love with.

Pushkin takes a great deal of comfort from the company of other dogs and becomes worried and stressed when left on her own. Because of this, she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help guide her through life. She gets along beautifully with other dogs and has happily shared kennels and enjoyed play dates with a variety of canine companions. She is respectful around toys and eats well alongside other dogs, making her an easy companion to have around.

She is now walking on a harness and has made lovely progress, although some things can still make her nervous when out and about. Her adopters will need to be patient and reassuring, helping her to feel safe and encouraging her when she encounters new experiences. She gains confidence from having another dog alongside her and would benefit from a calm canine friend to help her navigate the world.

Pushkin has never experienced life in a home before, so her new family will need to be kind, patient and understanding as she learns all about home life. She will need help with house training and learning the everyday routines that most pet dogs take for granted. She enjoys treats, so positive reinforcement will be a wonderful way to help her learn and build confidence. She will need a home with adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. We would consider homing her with dog savvy teenagers 13+. She will also need a secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft to ensure her safety while she adjusts to her new home.

Pushkin is a special little lady who has so much love to give. With plenty of patience, reassurance and the support of a canine friend, she will continue to blossom into a wonderful companion. She has brought so much joy to those caring for her, and we know that the lucky family who adopts her will absolutely adore her.

She has been treated for a ear infection.

Pushkin has been given the Gift of Life by Cherry Lewis

The last two weeks or so Pushkin, along with her kennel buddy Maggie, has been joining the big play group down the big play yard everyday (weather permitted) and she absolutely loves it. She enjoys saying hello to the other doggies there and play chases with some of them, it's so cute to watch, it makes my heart melt. It's amazing to see how much her confidence has grown, she really is blossoming.

She is quite attached to me, and does get excited to see me, she loves getting fusses from me, and is never too far from where I am if we're in a yard together, so if you like having a little extra shadow following you around she could be the girl for you.I took her out today on just a lead instead of a harness and she did amazingly, that being said for safety reasons and until she is comfortable and feels safe with you adopters would need to walk her on a harness for a while.Pushkin is just an amazing girl, I can't praise her enough and I'm always more than happy to talk about her with anyone who is interested in adopting her.

This beautiful lady brightens up my days, and as this has been a difficult week for me personally, she has been there to put a smile on my face through it.She can be nervous when you meet her initially but her confidence has grown so much she just needs time to warm up to you and figure you out, but once she's comfortable and her personality comes out she's just so much fun, and so loving. She has such a quirky personality and I absolutely adore her.Pushkin does walk on a harness, although some things do make her nervous still when out on a walk so adopters will need to be aware of this and let her know she is safe as well as some encouragement.Pushkin gets along with pretty much all dogs, any dog she has been kennelled with or introduced to for a play date she has always been so good, is fine with toys around and also eats well around the other dogs.She has never lived in a home before so her new family will have to show her the ropes and help her with her house training, be encouraging and use positive reinforcement, she does enjoy treats so they should be a big help.I'm not lying when I say I genuinely get excited to see her everyday I'm at work, she really is a little ray of sunshine.

Pushkin has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for a loving forever home. She is initially quite nervous and unsure, but once you spend some time with her she starts to come out of her shell and even begins to enjoy a fuss.

Pushkin is a sweet girl who simply needs understanding and the chance to build her confidence at her own pace. She will be looking for a calm and quiet home where she can settle in gradually and continue to blossom. She takes a great deal of comfort from the company of other dogs and becomes quite worried and stressed when left on her own. Because of this, she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and show her that the world isn't such a frightening place.

Pushkin has never experienced life in a home before, so her new family will need to be kind, patient and understanding as she learns all about home life and new skills such as house training. She has made lovely progress with her harness training and is now walking on a harness, although she is still a little nervous when out and about. She is much more confident when she has another dog alongside her, so having a calm canine companion to help reassure her on walks will be a real benefit. She will need a home with adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She will also need a secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft to ensure her safety while she adjusts to her new home.

With plenty of love, reassurance and the support of a canine friend, Pushkin will continue to grow in confidence and become a wonderful companion. She is a lovely girl with so much potential, and we can't wait to see her enjoying the happy life she truly deserves.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Nora
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I’m new to walking on a harness and doing well!

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

Nora is a gentle girl who has come to us from a breeder and is now in foster, where she has been able to experience life in a home for the first time. She has been in foster for over a month now, and this has given us a much better understanding of her mobility, as well as allowing her confidence to grow and her lovely personality to shine through.

Nora is still very mistrustful of people, but she is beginning to show us that she really does want to make friends. She is now much more willing to approach her fosterer and has recently started coming over to take treats from her. She will even jump up onto the sofa to watch Netflix, as long as there is another dog already on the sofa with her! These may seem like small things, but for Nora they are huge steps forward and show just how much she is beginning to relax. She will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her home that will allow her to lean on them as she continues to settle.

She absolutely loves the comforts of home life and takes great reassurance from having other dogs around her. She has also been on a few short walks outside the home, allowing her to slowly experience the world beyond her garden. She is still a very sensitive girl and everything will need to be introduced gradually, but she is making lovely progress.

Nora's mobility has also improved in a home setting. Her ataxia appears to be closely linked to her stress levels and is much more noticeable when she is worried or overwhelmed. When she is relaxed, her movements are almost normal, which is incredibly encouraging. She is not currently on any medication, and her fosterer is helping her to build muscle strength through daily massage and gentle exercise.

Nora will need a quiet and understanding home with adopters who have experience with nervous dogs and, ideally, ex-breeders. She will need at least one calm, friendly resident dog to give her confidence and show her the way. Her new family will need to be incredibly patient and allow her to settle and build trust at her own pace, without expecting too much too soon.

Nora has had lots of hardships in her life and is still learning that she can feel safe around people. However, the progress she has made since moving into foster has been wonderful to see. Beneath her worries is a very sweet girl who is slowly discovering how lovely life can be, and we are hoping that the right home will give her the security, patience and love she needs to continue blossoming.

Nora has been given the Gift of Life by Judie Fisher

Nora has been in foster for over a month now which allowed us to have a good assessment of her mobility, and also helped increase her confidence and introduce her to living in a home. This gentle girl has a very sweet personality and loves the comforts of home life and the company of other dogs. She is still very mistrustful of humans, but I can see that she is now more willing to try and be friends. She has recently started coming up to take a treat from me, and will even jump up on the sofa to watch Netflix with me (as long as there is another dog on the sofa too). She has also been on a few short walks outside to see the world beyond my home and garden!

Nora's ataxia has improved in a home setting too, largely because it is connected to her mental state and seems to be worse when she is stressed. When Nora is relaxed, her movements are almost normal, which is lovely to see and gives me hope that once she feels safe and comfortable mentally, she will have a great quality of life. We just need to help her get there. Nora is not on any medication at the moment, but I massage her daily and we are working on building her muscle strength.

Nora's ideal home will be a quiet setting with one or more calm and friendly dogs. Her people will need to be kind and very patient, with experience of scared dogs and preferably beagles too. This gorgeous girl has had lots of hardships in her life, it is time for her to finally have a place where she feels safe and loved.

I have been working with Nora a few days a week since she first arrived with us and was on medication and crate rest for her legs. Around two weeks ago, Nora moved to a different section, so I haven't seen her in a little while. I popped over today to check in and chat to one of her new kennel dads to see how she's doing.

Since arriving on her new section, Nora has made huge leaps! She is now harness-trained and wears her harness comfortably during the day. She has grown more confident with handling and with walking on her harness to and from the yard, though she is not yet feeling up to walks outside the centre. She also now sits curiously at the front of her kennel, watching people and dogs come and go on her section, rather than hiding in the back.

Nora still has a long way to go in learning to trust humans and receive our love, but she's made huge steps already. It's a great reminder that all of us working here have different skills, and sometimes a dog who is struggling just needs a change of scene to take the next steps in their journey towards their forever home.

Nora is so gentle and if you ignore the deep defensive howl (she is a beagle after all!) eventually she quietens down and she shows her soft side.Nora is still trying to get used to enjoying human company. She is not there yet but is slowly beginning to show signs of trusting people and does settle near you with a little patience.

It appears to me that it's not that Nora dislikes people, it's more a matter of how she is unsure of who we are and how we do things.

Once she  settles and it does take a little time, although still afraid, is much more willing to be approached by people.

In this calmer state, I was able to smooth her coat all over and gently stroke her without her worrying too much which is a positive step for her.

Nora will need this gentle approach for some time but the reward will be endless love and loyalty which is priceless.

I believe all Nora needs right now is the stability and security that a loving home can offer.Nora does much prefer the company of dogs  at the moment so it is a must that there is a resident dog already in the home for her to be with.

Nora has kennelled with small dogs but we do feel she would be better placed with a dog of a similar size or larger.

Our next step whilst Nora is with us will be to train her to walk on a harness so she can start to discover and enjoy the outside world.

Nora has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is a scared girl who is understandably feeling overwhelmed to find herself here and is desperately in need of kindness, patience and TLC as she begins to settle and learn that the world can be a safe place.

When Nora first arrived with us, she was showing some neurological symptoms and ataxia, and her back legs would occasionally slide from underneath her, causing her to stumble. Following investigations with our vets, it was found that her proprioception was delayed in all four limbs. She was trialed on a course of medication alongside crate rest and has made wonderful progress. Her proprioception is now normal, she is able to get around and play happily, and she enjoys life much more comfortably. She does still have a slight amount of ataxia and can occasionally limp still. Our vet feels that she may have suffered an acute injury at some point in the past which has largely resolved itself, though she will likely never present like a normal dog.

Nora will be looking for adopters who will love and cherish her just as she is. Due to her mobility history, she will need a home without slippery flooring, or one where plenty of rugs and runners are in place to help her move around confidently and safely.

She would be best suited to a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs and understand her worries. Nora will need time to settle at her own pace and will thrive with patient adopters who are happy to let her progress in her own time. She takes great comfort from the company of other dogs and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to show her the way and help her build confidence.

Nora has never experienced life in a home before so her new family will need to be understanding as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and initially she will need to practise wearing her harness and exploring safely within the home and garden before she is ready to venture further afield.

Although Nora is still very worried and unsure of the world around her, beneath her fears is a sweet and deserving little girl who simply needs someone to believe in her. Watching a scared dog slowly learn to trust is one of the most rewarding experiences, and with love, patience and understanding, Nora will blossom. The day she greets you with a wagging tail and a sparkle in her eyes will make every moment of that journey worthwhile.

name: Nicole
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

Nicole has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for her forever home. She was very scared when she first arrived and had clearly had little handling or socialisation, making human contact very worrying for her.

Nicole briefly moved into a foster home to learn about home life but returned to us following one incident where she became tangled in her lead and harness, panicked and nipped her fosterer. This was a single incident during a frightening experience, but adopters must understand that she can panic if she feels trapped or overwhelmed.

Nicole has now been back at the rescue for just over a month and is making lovely progress. She still doesn't like being picked up or handled, but is much better than she was and is increasingly comfortable spending time around people she trusts. She enjoys sitting in the play yard with her trusted people and responds brilliantly to treats, which are helping to build her confidence. She is a curious, cheeky little character who loves food, toys and snoozing in her bed, and she is even trying hard to be kennel clean.

Nicole loves other dogs and takes comfort from their presence, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog to help her feel secure and act as a role model.

She needs a calm, quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs. As she has never successfully experienced home life, she will need patience with house training and learning the basics of being a pet. Lead and harness training will also need to be introduced very carefully because of her previous experience.

Nicole still has a long way to go, but her curiosity and wonderful personality are beginning to shine through. With the right home, canine companion and plenty of time and understanding, we hope she will continue to blossom.

Our vets noted a slightly unusual heart rhythm, and a heart scan showed mild valve changes. She currently requires no treatment and is expected to live a normal, happy life, although routine heart checks and monitoring for future symptoms are recommended. She has been treated for a ear infection.

Nicole has been given the Gift of Life by Shirley Bourne

Nicole has been back at the rescue with me for just over a month now, and even though she is still a scared lady, I can definitely see she has made progress. She still doesn’t like to be picked up and handled, but she’s a lot better with it now than she was when she first arrived. She’s also more content just being in my presence now and will happily hang out with me in the play yard with confidence. I spend a lot of time sitting on the floor with her and dishing out treats every so often to stay in her good books. She does love her food, so this helps massively with building some trust with her!

Nicole does still have a long way to go until she’s anywhere near being a ‘normal’ dog, but she has a lot of curiosity in her and definitely some Shih Tzu attitude as well, so I’m hoping she will blossom in the right home. If you have lots of time and patience, and a space in your heart and home to welcome a special lady, please consider Nicole. I promise you won’t regret it!

Nicole is the type of dog that can instantly put a smile on your face, even when she’s not doing anything. She has such a comical and infectious energy, and I really just love spending time with her. She loves snoozing in bed in her kennel through the day and playing with toys too. She even tries her hardest to be kennel clean!! She’s very easy to look after day to day. So please… give her a chance.

Nicole has been in foster for a week and is a sweetie. She has a wonderfully inquisitive nature and loves investigating everything around her, which makes us chuckle! She is still very nervous about being handled and will bark when she's feeling unsure, but she is already making progress. She now takes treats from us and absolutely loves her food. She is also mostly clean overnight.

Nicole has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for her forever home. She is a lovely little girl who is understandably feeling very scared and overwhelmed to find herself here. It’s clear she hasn’t had much handling or socialisation before, so human hands are quite worrying for her at the moment, but we will continue gently helping her learn that hands can be kind.

Nicole will be looking for a calm and quiet adult only home where she can settle in at her own pace. She would really benefit from adopters who have experience with nervous ex-breeding dogs and who understand the patience, time and reassurance she will need as she learns to trust.

She loves other dogs and takes great comfort from their presence, so Nicole will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help her feel safe and secure.

As Nicole has never lived in a home before, she will need patient adopters who are ready to help her learn everything about home life from the very beginning. She will need to learn new skills like house training and will also need to learn all about walking on a lead and harness.

With time, kindness and plenty of TLC, Nicole will begin to grow in confidence and let her personality shine.

Our vets have noted that Nicole has a slightly unusual heart rhythm, so she underwent a heart scan at our vets which showed some mild valve changes. At this stage she does not require any treatment and is expected to live a normal, happy life, although we would recommend routine heart checks and monitoring for any future symptoms.

description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

27-08-26 Sianon has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for her forever home. She is a worried girl who is unsure around humans and isn't used to being handled yet. She is going to need plenty of love, patience and TLC as she settles in and slowly begins to grow in confidence.

Sianon will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who understand that she will need time to adjust. Her new family will need to be kind and patient, allowing her to settle in at her own pace without putting pressure on her. She has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her, and she will need gentle guidance as she learns all about home life and new skills such as house training and how to walk on a lead and harness.

Sianon relies on other dogs for confidence, so she will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and help her feel safe. We hope having a canine companion by her side will help her learn that the world isn't such a scary place. Any children in the home will need to be teenagers aged 16+.

Sianon is a gentle girl who has lots to learn, but with the right home, a patient family and a lovely canine friend to show her the ropes, we hope she will gradually discover her confidence and enjoy all the wonderful things life has to offer.

Sianon has been given the Gift of Life by Dee Wickson-Dix

name: Dutch
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who respect my space.

I need to be the only dog in my new home. No cats please!

I walk well on a lead and muzzle trained. I would enjoy an active lifestyle!

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I am already vaccinated and neutered and ready for my new home!

Dutch is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a pound in Ireland in search of a fresh start. Unfortunately, we don't know much about his history, but what we do know is that he is one of the most loving and affectionate dogs you could ever hope to meet, with a heart as big as his personality. Dutch simply wants to be close to his people, whether that's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up beside you for cuddles. Being with the people he loves is all he really wants.

Dutch would love to find a home with adopters who are around for most of the day and can include him in everyday life. He thrives on human companionship and will make a wonderfully devoted shadow to his new family. He will need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and understand typical breed traits, including prey drive and the need for appropriate mental and physical enrichment.

Dutch would be best suited to life as an only dog. Although he can socialise well with other dogs of a similar size, he can become overexcited and mouthy, which may lead to frustration. Because of this, he is muzzle trained and wears a muzzle during social interactions to help him continue building positive experiences. He cannot live with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need support with house training and learning the general routines of family life. He is such a clever boy and always tries his very best to do the right thing, so we are confident he will enjoy learning with patient, positive guidance.

Dutch already walks well on a lead, although he can occasionally be reactive when passing other kennels. This is understandable in a busy rescue environment and may be something his adopters will need to continue working on. He is an energetic, happy-go-lucky boy who is more than ready to start exploring the world with his new family. An active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, training and quality time with his people would suit him perfectly.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate that he will need a gentle introduction to his new surroundings and his own space to settle in.

Dutch is bright, affectionate and full of love. He has so much to offer and is simply looking for someone to love as much as he loves them. For the right family, he will be an incredibly loyal, fun-loving and devoted companion.

Dutch has a passport and travel document.

Dutch has been given the Gift of Life by Louise Southward

I still can’t quite understand how this incredibly smart and loving boy hasn’t found his forever home yet.If you’re looking for a dog to train, learn new tricks and go on lots of adventures with, then Dutch really is your boy.He’s the best of both worlds a crazy, energetic boy who also absolutely loves his people and loves nothing more than a good snuggle.

Dutch, or as I like to call him, Dutchy, is honestly one of the most loving and affectionate boys you could ever hope to meet.

He's the kind of dog who just wants to be close to you. Whether it's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up for cuddles, being with his people is all he really wants. Watching him have to go back into his kennel after spending time together is heartbreaking because kennel life is just no place for a boy like him.

What makes it even sadder is that he hasn't received a single application. If I'm honest, my biggest worry is that he'll become one of our long-stay dogs, and my heart breaks at the thought of that because he simply doesn't deserve it.

He's such a clever boy and always tries so hard to do the right thing. He recently went on his first long walk with one of our wonderful regular volunteers and was an absolute angel. He took everything in his stride and made everyone so proud.

He's also been having play dates with our lovely girl, Swanny, to help him burn off some of that doggy energy while learning good doggy manners.

At the end of the day, Dutchy is just a baby. He's got the biggest heart, so much love to give, and he deserves a home where he'll be someone's whole world instead of waiting behind kennel doors. I know his family is out there somewhere; I just hope they find him before he spends another day wondering why no one has chosen him.

Dutch is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a pound in Ireland in search of a fresh start. Unfortunately, we don't know much about his history, but what we do know is that he is one of the most loving and affectionate dogs you could ever hope to meet.

He would love to find a loving home with adopters who are around most of the time and would have plenty of time to spend with him. He would need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and experience with his typical breed traits like prey drive etc.

Dutch would be best suited to being homed as an only dog as although he does socialise well with other dogs of his size, he can become over excited and mouthy which can lead to frustration. For this reason he is being trained to wear a muzzle when socialising. He cannot be homed with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. With patience and guidance, we think he will adapt well and enjoy all the comforts a home has to offer.

Dutch can already walk well on a lead, though he can be a little reactive when passing other kennels, this is understandable in a busy rescue environment, but may be something his adopters will need to work with him on. He is an energetic and incredibly lovely bo who ie is happy-go-lucky in nature and is more than ready to start adventuring with his new adopters. He would love an active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, and quality time with his people.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate and understand that he will need a gentle and quiet introduction to the home, along with his own space to settle in.

He is a bright, affectionate, and fun-loving boy who is sure to make a wonderful and loyal companion for a lucky family.

name: Lollipop
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 +, who respect my space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home and would prefer a male dog. I don't mind cats!

I'm new to lead walking and need some practice!

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have a grade 2 luxating patella and have had 7 teeth extracted. Read below for more

Lollipop is a lovely Bichon Frise who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is an inquisitive and funny little girl who is already showing glimpses of her playful personality. Lollipop will happily come over to lick our fingers before darting away again, as if she's still deciding whether people are quite as interesting as her kennel friends.

Lollipop is still a nervous little girl, but she has been making lovely progress and is gradually becoming more curious about the people around her. The more time you spend with her, the more interested she becomes in you, and it is lovely to see her slowly coming out of her shell.

Lollipop loves the company of other dogs and relies heavily on them for comfort and reassurance. She is happy to follow their lead and takes great confidence from having another dog around. For this reason, she will need to have a resident dog in her new home. She will be looking for a home with a male resident dog as she can sometimes be a little sassy with female dogs.

Lollipop has also been making lovely progress with her harness training. She is easy to put her harness on and recently went out for her very first walk. Considering how nervous she can be, she did incredibly well! She will need plenty more gentle practice to help her become confident and comfortable with walking, and her adopters will need to continue this at her own pace.

As Lollipop has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to a whole new world and gains confidence in her surroundings.

Lollipop could share her home with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who can appreciate and understand that she will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and her own space to settle in.

She has arrived with a Grade 2 luxating patella, but her mobility appears unaffected and this may improve as she builds muscle tone. Lollipop has also arrived with severe periodontal disease and has had seven teeth extracted.

Lollipop is an active and spritely little girl with a bright future ahead of her. With the support of a kind canine friend and a patient family, we hope her confidence will continue to grow and her charming personality will shine through even more.

Lollipop has been given the Gift of Life by Jodie Stanley

Lollipop is a lovely lady, she’s doing ever so well here and making great progress in confidence. She loves going out for a stroll or bouncing around with her friends in our yards. Lollipop also loves to sunbath as seen in her photos.

Lollipop still has a way to go in terms of confidence with humans and is looking for a gentle adult only home with where there will be a doggie (male as she can be a little sassy with female dogs)  companion. Lollipop really is a sweet, funny and  gentle lady, and so ready for a proper home.

Lollipop has been making lovely progress with her harness training. Today, she went out for her very first walk and, considering she is still quite a nervous girl, she did incredibly well. She is easy to put her harness on, but she will need plenty more practice to help her become confident and comfortable with walking.

Lollipop relies heavily on her kennel friends for reassurance, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help her settle into family life. The more time you spend with her, the more curious she becomes about you, and it is lovely to see her gradually coming out of her shell.

She definitely prefers the company of other dogs at the moment, but she is happy to follow their lead and takes great comfort from having them around. As Lollipop gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends, she will need a kind resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Lollipop has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to a whole new world and gains confidence in her surroundings.

Lollipop could share her home with older dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who can appreciate and understand that she will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and her own space to settle in.

She has arrived with a Grade 2 luxating patella but her mobility appears unaffected and this may improve as she builds muscle tone. Lollipop has also arrived with severe periodontal disease and has had 7 teeth extracted.

Lollipop is an active and spritely little girl with a bright future ahead of her. With the support of a canine friend and a patient family, we hope her confidence will continue to grow and her charming personality will shine through even more.

name: Max
description:
I need an active, breed experienced home that loves playtime!

I’m active and would love a large, secure garden to let off steam.

I walk on the lead but I can pull when excited.

I am house trained but I need to learn some manners.

I have been neutered and am ready for my forever home!

Max is a superstar Lurcher who has been returned to us from his adoptive family. They made the heartbreaking decision to bring him back as he was becoming dominant over the other dog in the home.

He is a very excitable, happy boy - essentially an overgrown puppy in a big body. Max is full of fun and enthusiasm and will need an active home that can meet his exercise and stimulation needs. He already knows some basic commands such as “sit”, “paw”, “lay down”, and “wait”, and he is eager to interact with his people. He is very food oriented, which makes training enjoyable and rewarding, and he already shows lovely food manners, waiting patiently when asked.

Max absolutely loves other dogs and gets incredibly excited when he sees a potential new friend. However, he is still young, full of energy, and not always aware of his size and strength. This can sometimes lead to him becoming overexcited, a little mouthy, and unintentionally overwhelming other dogs. He has been working hard on his social skills and has been socialising while wearing a muzzle for safe and positive interactions. This is purely as a precaution, and his future adopters will need to continue this training and take a responsible approach when introducing him to other dogs.

As he was too much for a more timid dog in his previous home, we feel that Max would be best suited to being homed as an only dog, provided he has plenty of appropriate socialisation with dogs of a similar size and play style. He cannot live with cats or small furries.

As Max has previously lived in a home, he is familiar with household sights and sounds and is house trained. However, he is still working on his lead manners and can pull when he gets excited. Ongoing training, structure, and consistency will be important, along with plenty of mental stimulation to keep his busy mind engaged. He would thrive in a home that can offer activities such as training games or even dog sports.

Max could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over, who understand that he can be a bit of a bull in a china shop. Any young people in the home will need to be confident and not worried by an enthusiastic dog who may jump up while he continues to work on his manners.

Max does struggle with separation anxiety and can become destructive if left alone for long periods, so he will need a home where someone is around most of the time and who is committed to helping him gradually build confidence with being left.

Max's new home will need a large, secure garden with 6ft boundaries, where he can let off some steam.

Max will make an amazing addition to a home with experience of similar breeds. He truly is a lovely boy, bouncy, affectionate, and full of life, with so much potential. He is a big-hearted lad who gives his whole heart, and with the right guidance, he will grow into an incredible companion.

Max has recently been castrated, and while he was feeling (understandably) sorry for himself for a few days after, he was brilliant going into the vets and during his recovery. Although he has had to wear a buster collar just to stop him licking at the area, he doesn't let that bother him and is such a good boy when you take it off to take him out for a walk and pop it back on when he's back in his kennel and he has been so easy to give his pain relief medication to as well, he really has been a model patient. He is such an easy dog to handle, given his size he is no issue at all.

During his recovery period, Max has only been on short walks so that he doesn't overdo it in the play yards, but slowly this past week he has been spending some time in our agility yard to have a run and you can definitely see that he is back to his full, playful self, running around, chasing a tennis ball and being inquisitive about anything and everything.

Max is a fantastic boy, and any time I spend with him is just so enjoyable and full of love and fun, he is such a special dog, I'm constantly scratching my head wondering why and how he's still here.

Where do I start with the wonderful ball of energy that is Max.

First and foremost, the question I ask myself and almost everyone that meets Max asks too, how on earth is he still waiting?! A young, handsome, intelligent dog who is BARRELS of fun. There’s something about Max that is just so loveable and he truly does capture people’s hearts. Many of the volunteers who walk him are always so happy to see him and enjoy their time together.

Recently we’ve been working on nailing a ‘touch’ command. When Max is focused he is such a rewarding dog to train. Sometimes his desire to please takes over and he waves his paw at me until I have to accept it (and of course reward because he's the goodest boy no matter what). He is also learning to be calmer when greeting people and has even had some gentle fuss from some children too. It remains true that Max cannot be homed with children under the age of 16, but it is so important for Max to have positive interactions with respectful children to prevent any reactivity / fear from developing. It also helps teach him to be calm when meeting new people, especially when they’re smaller than him!

Max brings such a unique type of energy to the rescue, he is such a joyful boy and truly comes alive when he is with his people. I threw Max a 1st birthday party and all of his favourite people came throughout the day to play with him and bring him yummy treats, fuss and cuddles. He had the best day and it was so touching to see how loved he is despite not being in a home.

We are doing our very best to raise Max into a well rounded, well socialised and well adjusted adult dog. However, he is at such a crucial stage in his development and has already spent 5 months in kennels. It’s no place for a young dog to grow up. Nearly half of his life spent in kennels patiently waiting for his second chance to come and take him home.

Despite his size Max really is just a baby and definitely a lap dog too. So if you have a spot on the sofa you can share, Max will happily join you and be the bestest friend anyone could wish for.

Myself and Max have formed a very close bond over the last few months we’ve been working together. We take daily walks, go to the big play yard and have plenty of cuddles and fusses.I’m not sure what it is about Max that keeps getting him overlooked, it could be his size or that he is like a big playful puppy or something else, whatever it is, anyone would be lucky to have this handsome chap in their lives, he will always put a smile on your face and he has such a good sense of humour, watching him having zoomies in his kennel yard while he’s jumping off the obstacles in there then stoping then going back round again is nothing short of entertaining, or when he’s fishing treats out of the paddling pool while simultaneously blowing bubbles with his nose.Max truly deserves the world, he is such a sweet and caring boy with a big personality and so much love to give, as well as his big size there is also a big heart and all he wants is to be able to fully give it to someone and finally find his forever home.

Max is a big, happy baby with bags of energy and so much love to give. He is an excitable, affectionate boy who adores attention and loves having people around him. He is always happy to greet you and be part of whatever is going on.

As Max is still young and growing, he is slowly learning his manners and how to greet people politely without jumping. . He will need adopters who can match his energy, continue his training, and give him the stimulation, guidance, and love he needs to thrive.

Max is a gentle, overlooked soul who is learning new things every day at the rescue, but he is missing the comforts of home. He cannot wait to find a family who understands him and can help him blossom into the wonderful companion he is meant to be.With the right home, patience, and plenty of love, Max will make a loyal and joyful best friend.

Since coming back into our care, Max has been working hard on learning how to socialise with other dogs. He absolutely adores them and gets incredibly excited when he sees a potential new friend! Because he’s still young, full of beans, and a bit unaware of his own size, he can sometimes be a little too enthusiastic. This can lead to him becoming overexcited, a bit mouthy, and unintentionally overwhelming other dogs.

To help him learn safe and positive interactions, Max has been socialising while wearing a muzzle. This is purely for his safety and that of other dogs, and his future adopters will need to continue this training and take a responsible approach when introducing him to new canine companions. Aside from that, Max is everything you’d want in a young pup he's bouncy, happy, affectionate, and full of life.

He’s very food oriented, which makes training a dream! He already knows commands like “sit” and has learned great food manners where be waits patiently until he’s told he can eat. Max thrives on mental stimulation and ongoing training, and with the right guidance, he has all the potential to grow into an incredible dog. Max does struggle with separation anxiety and can become destructive if left alone for long periods. He really craves human company so he’ll need a home where someone is around most of the time and is committed to helping him build confidence being alone gradually. He’s such a loving, handsome boy who gives his whole heart, and it would be wonderful to see him back in a home environment where he can truly thrive. As a young pup, he’s missed out on some important early experiences, so a patient, committed family will make all the difference in helping him become the best version of himself.

He is a very excitable, happy boy - essentially an overgrown puppy in a big body. Max is full of fun and enthusiasm and will need an active home that can meet his exercise and stimulation needs. He already knows some basic commands such as “sit”, “paw”, “lay down”, and “wait”, and he is eager to interact with his people.

Max loves other dogs but is often unaware of his size and strength, having grown into such a big lad very quickly. As he is still just a puppy, he is still learning about manners and can be mouthy and plays in a very typical Lurcher way. In his previous home, there was an incident when he was around 3 months old, where he was a little too rough and resulted in a small dog needing veterinary treatment. He has started muzzle training for off-lead play as a precaution, and he will need a home that understands Lurcher play styles and is confident managing this appropriately. We have been socialising him with dogs of all sizes on walks and he is doing very well.

As Max has previously lived in a home, he is familiar with household sights and sounds and is house trained. However, he is still working on his lead manners and can pull when he gets excited. Ongoing training and consistency will be important.

Max will make an amazing addition to a home with experience of similar breeds. He truly is a lovely boy. He is a big-hearted, affectionate lad who is still convinced he can curl up and fit on your lap.

name: Criss Cross
description:
I need an adult-only experienced home that understands me.

I'd prefer to be the only dog in the home and no cats please!

I’m still shy, so I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I can now walk on a lead and harness and enjoy my walks.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home!

Meet Criss Cross, a big-hearted, sensitive lad who has come to us from a breeder and is slowly learning to find his confidence in the world. When Criss Cross arrived as a worried soul, needing extra patience, understanding, and gentle care. He had very little formal handling in his past, and early on could be grumbly or anxious when unsure. He required slow, careful introductions to people, places, and experiences while he started to understand his new surroundings.

While Criss Cross can still be a little shy when meeting new people, once he feels comfortable his affectionate side really shines through. He actively seeks out fuss and cuddles and has become quite the cuddle bug, often trying to return kisses to the people he trusts. He is learning his manners well and responds nicely to calm, consistent guidance.

Criss Cross is growing in confidence with his harness training and now enjoys daily walks beyond the rescue. He has even started greeting some people on his walks for a hello and perhaps a treat or a fuss. He can still feel a little unsure if people are behind him, but gentle encouragement and reassurance help him relax and continue exploring the world around him.

He has also started learning about kennel cleanliness, with staff helping him practice good toilet habits to make the transition into a home life easier for him in the future. When enjoying some quiet time on his own, Criss Cross loves exploring his toy collection, especially anything involving treats or food puzzles.

Criss Cross would prefer to be the only dog in the home so he can fully relax and enjoy all the attention for himself.

He will need a calm, adult-only home with experienced adopters who can continue helping him build confidence at his own pace. He also appreciates having a quiet space at mealtimes where he feels safe and secure. Criss Cross will need a home without cats as he is overly interested in them.

Criss Cross is a truly gorgeous, sweet-natured gentle giant with so much love to give. With patience, understanding, endless bum scratches and plenty of tasty treats, he has every chance to flourish into the loyal and devoted companion he is meant to be.

Criss Crosswill need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Criss Cross is the most sensitive soul who is easily affected by life and it breaks my heart, he's looking for a very special human who would take him under their wing and give him all that he needs to thrive and cope with how scary the world can be. Whilst his best friend Crumble has been on kennel rest Criss Cross has really been struggling to be brave enough to go for road walks, he's only felt comfortable walking around the quiet field that's behind his section as he can cope with it there and he feels safe. Since Crumble has been given the go ahead to start going for little walks daily again he has been enjoying his road walks in her company. This just highlights how sensitive he is and how much he struggles in certain situations. He did go for a couple of walks with a collie but he didn't get much comfort from her company so didn't really enjoy them.I know he needs a very specific person who will love him exactly for who he is and who has the right set up to help him have a truly wonderful life as he deserves. I just hope they're out there somewhere looking for a big bundle of love who just needs some understanding to be able to help his cheeky and funny personality shine through.

Criss Cross has been doing very well socialising with other dogs, he walks politely next to calm dogs and even had a muzzled play date the other day. His best friend Crumble is currently on kennel rest, so he only gets to see her very briefly whilst on lead, but he always runs to the front of her kennel to say hello before going back to his own kennel.

He is such a sweet boy who adores his people once he trusts you. He just needs positive introductions to feel comfortable with new people. Very proud of the progress he's been making and we'll continue to work on his doggy social skills.

Criss Cross is such a sweetheart! He is loyal to his friend Crumble, his kennel mums and dads. He’s still greeting everyone on walks with a bit of caution but once he’s recognised you, you’re considered family.

He’s going on occasional independent walks to gain his confidence but he is always looking for Crumble to keep him company. He’s very cautious of new things however day by day his confidence is growing and with his trust in his kennel mums he always runs back to check they’re okay, showing you just how brave he is and continues to be, so when the right home finds him….they will have to earn his trust and give him the patience and love he truly deserves.

This distinguished gent is progressing so well, every day!

He has started to get in the practice of being kennel clean, one of his kennel mums likes to come in a little early to help him practice this so when he finds his forever home it might be a little less stressful learning toilet training skills properly.

Criss Cross is even getting more adventurous greeting people on his daily walks now just to  say hello and maybe scoring a treat or fuss, and even recognising some of the staff when they visit him.

He is protective of Crumble and always looks to see her catching up on their daily walks, and enjoys playing with her or being near watching over her. But when he has his solo kennel time, he has been exploring his personal toy collection, anything with a treat in it and he’s happy. This cuddle bug deserves a home with endless bum scratches and scrumptious treats

This handsome guy is progressing every day! And showing his kennel mums just how much of a sweetheart he is. He is an affectionate goofball once he’s comfortable with you. He enjoys playing with his chow friend Crumble and he loves getting love from her and his kennel mums. He loves to jump up to have his harness put on, refusing to stand still because he gets so excited to go out and explore with Crumble.

Criss Cross will now even allow some of his part time kennel mums and dads to give him attention too. He is still very cautious of new people but is slowly meeting new people and remembering them!

With some time his new family will find out just how special Criss Cross is!

Criss Cross has made incredible progress over the last few days. He used to hide and grumble when people approached his kennel, but this has changed massively!

Now, Criss Cross comes up to the kennel door and wags his tail, getting very excited to see people. Spending time with this handsome boy brings me so much joy; I often find myself straying from my section just to sneak in five minutes of cuddles.

Criss Cross is still looking for a quiet, gentle home and someone who will take things slow while he gets to know them.

Criss-Cross has grown into an incredibly sociable and interactive boy, although he can still be a little shy when first meeting new people. Once he feels comfortable, he actively seeks out attention and loves a cuddle, often trying to give kisses in return. Criss-Cross is a big lad and is still learning his manners; when he’s excited he can occasionally use his size to try and barge past, but he responds well to clear, firm verbal guidance.

He will need a quiet area to enjoy his meals, as this helps him feel more secure. Criss-Cross is doing very well with his harness training and has already ventured out of the rescue for walks, managing a good distance down the road. He can still feel a little unsure if people are walking behind him, and one of his endearing little quirks is that he finds reassurance if you turn and face him while walking backwards. Criss-Cross is a truly gorgeous, sweet and gentle giant who will thrive in an active, patient and understanding home.

Criss Cross is a very worried soul who has come to us from a breeder, and is needing extra patience, understanding, and tender care. He appears to have had very little formal handling in his past and can be grumbly or anxious when he feels uncomfortable. He requires slow, careful introductions and time to begin to understand the world around him.

Criss Cross would thrive in an adult-only home with experienced owners who can provide the reassurance and consistency he needs to start building trust. He is still learning the basics of house training and walking on a lead, so his adopters will need to be patient and gentle as he gradually discovers confidence. He will need an understanding and kind resident dog in the home he can look to as he continues to learn and trust.

This sweet, sensitive boy is not yet ready for the full bustle of the world, but with time, quiet encouragement, and safe garden sniffing adventures, he will slowly open up and reveal the loyal companion he can be. Criss Cross will need a calm, loving home where his cautious nature is respected and nurtured and where he can finally feel safe and truly belong.

name: Jinx
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need a secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have a sore eye that is being monitored.

22-09-26 Jinx is an exceptionally frightened boy who has come into our care from a breeder.

He will do all he can to run away and hide from us, and it is heartbreaking to witness just how scared he is. Despite his trust issues, he has allowed a small amount of fuss, although he remains very wary and unsure of our intentions. He will need lots of time, patience and gentle handling while he learns that he is safe.

Because of this, Jinx will need another kind and confident dog in his new home, and this dog will be a much-needed support system for him as he begins to settle and gain some confidence.

We have not yet cat tested Jinx, but given what we have seen from him so far, it is unlikely that he would be suitable to share a home with cats.

As Jinx has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. He will need a quiet, experienced home with adopters who understand ex-breeding dogs and are prepared to be very patient with him.

Due to his nervous nature, Jinx is currently a flight risk and will need a very secure garden with boundaries of at least 6ft. He is a very scared boy and may need to be muzzled for formal handling eg. vet visits.

Jinx has arrived with a sore eye, so we are keeping on top of cleaning it and making sure he is comfortable while we assess this further.

Jinx has a long way to go, but the fact that he has already allowed a little fuss shows that there is a gentle side beneath all those worries. We hope that with the right canine companion, experienced adopters and lots of patience, he will slowly learn to trust and discover the safe and loving life he deserves.

Jinx has been given the Gift of Life by Lesley Beattie

name: Bella
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need a secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I've started my vaccinations and will be spayed before adoption.

22-09-26 Bella is a frightened girly who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start.

She is showing little glimpses of curiosity, but is very flighty at the moment. She will not yet approach us and will try to run away if she feels she can. Once cornered, Bella shuts down and accepts handling, although she is clearly very unsure of what is happening around her.

At the moment, Bella is feeling a little less brave and is finding comfort in the company of her kennel friends. We feel it would be best for Bella to be rehomed with another dog for support and companionship. That said, we will continue to assess her confidence while she is with us to see whether she could eventually adapt to being an only dog.

As Bella has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. She will need an adult-only home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who understand the patience and understanding she will need.

Due to her nervous nature Bella will need a very secure garden with 6ft fencing to keep her safe.

Bella has a worried little soul, but those glimpses of curiosity give us hope that there is a more confident girl waiting to emerge. With time, patience and the reassurance of a kind canine companion, we hope she can begin to feel safe, find her paws and enjoy the fresh start she deserves.

Bella has been given the Gift of Life by Olivia Coles

name: Pippa
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need an extra secure garden to keep me safe.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I'm fully vaccinated and will be spayed before adoption.

30-09-26 Pippa is a very scared and nervous lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is very worried about being handled and becomes stressed if we attempt to pick her up. She will try to jump from our arms and, because of this, we would consider her a flight risk and she will need fencing of at least 6ft in her new garden to keep her safe. She will need very careful handling and adopters who understand just how frightened she is at the moment.

Pippa gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Pippa has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be very patient and give her time to adjust to all the new sights, sounds and experiences that come with living in a home.

Pippa will need a quiet, confident, adult-only home where she can relax and settle into her new surroundings without too much hustle and bustle. Her adopters will need to have ex-breeding experience and understand her nervous nature and allow her to progress at her own pace.

Pippa is a very worried girl right now, but with the security of a kind canine companion and a calm, patient family, we hope she will slowly begin to feel safe and gain the confidence she needs to enjoy her new life.

Pippa has been given the Gift of Life by Margaret Hunter

name: Gabriel
description:
I need an adult-only experienced home that understands me.

I would need to be the only animal in the home.

I may be shy now, but once I have settled I would love a nice garden I can play in!

I love going for walks, and would love an active home!

I know some tricks & walk well on the lead but will need help with housetraining.

I have been neutered and am ready to find my forever home.

Gabriel originally came to us from a breeder, and for him the world felt like a very frightening place. He was worried of people, and new environments and unfamiliar experiences left him feeling overwhelmed. Even something as simple as having a lead put on was a huge challenge. He needed time, patience and gentle encouragement to begin to feel safe.

Gabriel was adopted for a short period, but unfortunately it was not the right fit for him. He was returned after displaying unwanted behaviours in the home and making the wrong choices when he felt uncomfortable in a situation, which did result in Gabriel biting. He will need a quiet, adult-only home without resident or visiting children. Gabriel can struggle with visitors coming to the house, so he will need a home without too many visitors and where he can be placed in a separate room when people do come over. His adopters will also need to be willing to meet him multiple times before adoption so that he has the opportunity to develop a bond and build trust with them.

Gabriel is a very sensitive boy who feels anxious about a lot of things. During his time here we are trying to help him feel more comfortable by giving him the tools to know how to be more relaxed in these scary situations. To Gabriel, new people are very scary and he feels that he needs to tell them to go away by barking and lunging, when put in poor situations this has led to him having a bite history. He is a very sweet dog but he has very little he trusts in this world and unfortunately humans are top of that list at the moment. With people who have earned his trust he is exceptionally sweet and loving, he loves to give you cuddles and he really thinks he should be a lap dog. When introductions are done slowly and in a manner that he can cope with he will allow that person into his circle reasonably quickly and then he gets very excited to see them.

As he has had very little in this world he does become exceptionally attached to his trusted humans and doesn't like to share them with other dogs or other people, so he is looking for a home with a maximum of two people and will need to be the only dog in the home. Adopters with experience of guarding behaviours are essential to help him succeed in his next home and make sure it really will be his forever home.

Gabriel walks nicely on his harness and gets very excited to see dogs when out and about but is wary of strangers walking past, for this reason he is muzzled when out as it keeps him safe in the event of someone getting too close or trying to touch him.

He has shown signs of resource guarding his food here and any high value long lasting treats. He has Kongs as he is happy for the empty Kong to be removed from his kennel once he feels he's finished with it, but these are things that will have to be managed in his new home. It would be a good idea to limit his access to the kitchen in the home to avoid the possibility of him getting things that he may be inclined to guard, especially until he settles and the bond has been built with him to ensure that he trusts that you won't take things away from him without him getting something higher value in its place.

Gabriel socialises well with other dogs here and does enjoy chasing dogs around our big play yard here, so having the opportunity to continue making friends with playful dogs in his new home is necessary to keep him happy and help him to continue to grow in confidence. Someone will be incredibly lucky to have Gabriel as their companion, they will just have to understand that he does require the time and effort to make sure he progresses and starts to see the world is less scary than he thinks it is.

Gabriel will need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Today I got to spend more time with Gabriel than I usually would so I took advantage of that and we went for a much longer walk.... As usual he was brilliant, he listens, if we need to move out of the way for a car he'll listen to me and move off the road to the side, if he's walking slightly ahead and I call him he stops and turns back.

We also sat around the other side of the rescue where it's usually busier as I want to get him used to being in busier areas and being around people he doesn't know, as he can be a bit reactive.... He did so well, it was fairly busy so he was a little unsure at first but the longer we stayed the better he was, he was good with others around him too, he has come such a long way, but this is something I'm going to keep on working on with him for the foreseeable as we don't know what life he'll have outside of here and he may need to used to busier areas.

We also played with a puzzle feeder today, which he decided would be fun to pick up with his mouth and drop it on the floor to get the treats out faster, he really is a funny boy, but he's super smart too and is quick to pick up tricks especially when there's treats involved.

He really is every Bocker lovers dream and he always gets so overlooked.

He is muzzle trained, and would need to wear his muzzle when meeting new people, dogs or at the vets, but he's also just a big softy who gives the loveliest cwtches and kisses, to be a part of his gang is such an amazing feeling and he shows his affection for you so clearly when he loves you.

This week we’ve had a heatwave which has meant alot of our rescue dogs have needed their ears checked incase they’ve had any mucky build up - Gabriel was one of the unlucky few that have needed some TLC in this area!!We’ve recently had a new meds person who has been visiting Gabriel to do his ear cleans & he has been an absolute angel. He’s even been given the nickname Angel GabrielIt’s just a testament to Gabriel that yes he can be unsure of new people, but once he knows you he truly is such a wonderful boy. He just needs someone to take that chance on him, show him the love he’s desperate to have & he’ll return it tenfold.Gabriel has been waiting such a long time now, and seeing a boy so full of love & hope is heartbreaking when we can’t reassure him that his time will come soon!!!

Today, I worked with Gabriel again for the first time in months. I was a little worried he’d have forgotten, however, it’s safe to say the bond previously made still remains.Gabriel is such an excited little boy. He lives for treats. He’s such a clever and obedient boy when the treats come out. Usually, he’s full of energy and excitement. Once the treats are out, he’s still and sits like the perfect little boy we know he can be.As he can be very busy, I’ve always thought it essential to take him out on walks, the longer the better. As mentioned in a previous update, he loves walks! Once you pull the lead out, you get a similar reaction to the treats.The longer the walk the better. Walks are so good for this gorgeous boy. They keep him stimulated and help shave off the pounds he gains from everyone giving him treats!On the whole, I was so happy to see my boy again. So happy, so loyal, keen to go on walks and he listened so well. I’m so proud of the progress he’s made since I last saw him!Gabriel still can be a challenge and, he does not like everyone. Once you’ve made that bond with him though, it stays. Don’t overlook this boy. He’s such a beautiful, intelligent and fun dog!

This boy has my heart, once you form that special bond with him I do believe it's for life. He is very loving and enjoys a cuddle and a fuss from people he feels comfortable around, as his adopter you'll hopefully get that bond through spending time with him and letting him go at his own pace.Gabriel, as most bockers do, lives for his food and treats, whenever I run him in from being in the yard I always leave a small treat in his bed or somewhere in the back for him to find, and he absolutely loves this he gets so excited knowing he'll get a treat and runs straight to the back of his kennel to find it.He loves his walks and his time in the big yard. He's the curious, adventurous type who just wants to investigate everything, a 10 minute stroll up the road can take us an extra 20-25 minutes to stroll back because he likes to explore, but I don't mind, seeing him happy makes me happy I'd never want to stop him from exploring the world.Gabriel would need an experienced, adult only home (view profile for explanation), he would need someone who is active and can provide him with mental and physical stimulation daily. He is a very smart boy and can pick things up quite quickly which is why, with the help from some treats I think he would pick up toilet training rather quickly.Please don't overlook this handsome guy just because he's not your small and fluffy type dog, Gabriel is a special boy with a lot of love to give, and for that right person/people he would become a true companion and best friend.

Gabriel, a stunning Bocker with a huge personality and an even bigger heart. This handsome boy is full of life and enthusiasm, always ready to embrace whatever the day brings. Gabriel thrives on affection and absolutely loves a good fuss and cuddle — he’s a real people-dog who enjoys being close to those he trusts.

Gabriel is a clever lad with so much potential. He’s already showing us just how intelligent he is as he responds to basic commands! With the right guidance and training , we know he’ll flourish and continue to grow in confidence, not that he lacks any confidence! He also walks beautifully on the lead, making him a joy to take out on adventures.

Sadly, Gabriel has been returned to us, and we are now searching for the right forever home where he can truly settle and feel secure. Gabriel would be best suited as an only dog, in a calm and quiet home environment. We are looking for a home with minimal visitors and no children, as busy households can feel overwhelming for him.

Gabriel can display guarding behaviours, so he will need experienced owners who understand this and can manage the home environment appropriately to support him. With the right knowledge, structure, and patience, Gabriel will thrive and continue to build trust.

Gabriel has so much love to give to the right person. With understanding, consistency, and kindness, he will make an incredibly loyal and devoted time

Gabriel is a stunning Bocker who is full of life, love, and character! This gorgeous boy is bursting with energy and adores nothing more than a good fuss and a cwtch.He’s incredibly smart, and we just know it wouldn’t take long for him to be trained to a very high standard – he’s already showing us how bright he is every day. Gabriel also walks beautifully on the lead, making him a joy to take out and about.Now all he needs is a forever family who can give him the love, attention, and adventures he deserves. With his brains, energy, and big heart, Gabriel is sure to make someone the most wonderful companion.

Gabriel has come to us from a breeder and has made incredible progress since arriving with us! When he first came, he was nervous around new people and worried about having a lead put on, which made walks and new kennel staff introductions a real challenge. Now, he gets excited for walk time and happily allows us to put on both his lead and harness with no issues.This handsome boy is a true foodie and loves learning new tricks. He already knows “sit” and “paw,” so with trust and patience, teaching him more tricks should be a fun and rewarding experience. Gabriel needs a confident, experienced, owner who will provide clear boundaries and structure, as he can be cheeky if he thinks he’s in charge as well as an adult-only home where he can continue to learn. Gabriel has the confidence to be an only dog in a home with can allow him the dedication and time he needs and will need a home with no cats or small furries.Once Gabriel knows and trusts you, he is affectionate, loyal, and loves nothing more than sharing his goofy charm. Underneath his shy moments, he is a beautiful boy with a heart full of love. He is looking for someone who will continue his training, set clear rules, and enjoy all the affection, loyalty, and joy he has to give.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Darren
description:
Darren came into our care as a stray so we don’t have any background information about him. He is looking for a very special home with someone who truly understands the unique personality and characteristics of the Shar – Pei Breed. Like many Shar -Pei’s, he is an independent character who enjoys doing things on his own terms. He isn’t fussed about being handled, fussed over or touched and prefers his own personal space respected. He needs an understanding owner who can recognise his body language, respect his boundaries and give him time to build trust at his own pace. Whilst he may not be a cuddly, affectionate dog, he has his own personality and charm.

He really enjoys getting out on walks and it’s great to see him perk up with excitement as soon as he spots the lead, it certainly is the highlight of his day! He is strong on the lead and does pull a lot so he will need more work in this area. He has socialised well with dogs out on walks and has shown that he can be comfortable out in  a group.

Darren needs an experienced adult only home, with no visiting children.

Darren is best suited to being the only dog in the home so he can have his own space.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Gaston
description:
Meet Gaston!  Gaston is looking for a patient, quiet and loving home where he can learn to feel safe and secure.  He can be a very timid and nervous boy when you first meet him, and when he feels unsure, he may show this by being a little growly.  However, once he begins to trust you and feels more comfortable in your company, a much sweeter side of Gaston starts to shine through. He is a friendly boy underneath those initial worries.  He just needs time, understanding and the chance to build a bond at his own pace.  Gaston is still unsure around new people, so he will need an owner who understands that trust cannot be rushed.  He needs someone who will be happy to take things slowly, give him the space he needs and never expect too much from him too soon.  With patience, kindness and consistency, Gaston will grow in confidence and learn that the world isn’t such a scary place after all.  One of Gaston’s favourite things is going out for walks!  He enjoys having a sniff about and walks nicely on the lead, making this a lovely way to spend time with him and continue building that all-important trust.  Gaston is also very unsure around other dogs, so he will need to be the only dog in the home, where he can have his own space and feel safe without the worry of sharing his environment with another canine companion.  Gaston is looking for a patient and understanding owner that will let him settle at his own pace, and is willing to give him the time and reassurance he needs to build his confidence.

As Gaston came into us as a stray, we have no previous history on him, and as he can be very nervous we feel he would be best rehomed where any children in the home are 16+ years.

name: Dolores
description:
